status: proposed vocabulary; not a validated benchmark ontology
instance_rule: Concept instance = human-defined relation + explicit spec binding + tool-measured finite input/observation gap. A quoted requirement alone is a binding, not new empirical information. An observed gap proves neither a bug nor feasibility/infeasibility.
dimension_rule: Dimension is an operational input axis, not another concept: cardinality, occurrence count, eligibility, equality-to-threshold, subset slack, position, tie structure, cancellation, empty eligible set. Values and support conditions are bound per task.

concepts.intent: Trong declared output collection, mỗi eligible input occurrence phải được giữ đúng multiplicity; không suy ra thứ tự từ relation này.
activation: sorted copy of all input items
exclude_or_ambiguous: all values nhưng không rõ occurrence hay distinct value: unknown binding
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind input collection, output projection, eligibility predicate (default all only if justified), value equality. Initial support: finite list[int], exact int excluding bool; hashable scalar equality for Counter.
concepts.observable_relation_scope: Counter(output) == Counter(eligible input) if full multiset preservation required; can inspect a single value count as necessary condition. Sorting order is separate. One valid violation falsifies this bound relation; equality on samples does not prove it.
concepts.minimal_contrast: Spec preserves occurrences: [2]→[2] versus [2,2]→[2,2]; sorted(set(xs)) returns [2] on second. Counter equality alone cannot catch a wrong order.
concepts.tool_gap_example: In base+replay rows, eligible duplicate count is always ≤1. Eligible multiplicity≥2 has 0 observations; feasibility not inferred from absence.
unsupported_failure_modes: unhashable/nan/custom equality
alias/identity semantics
filter predicate unclear
dedup in unused variable or unreachable branch is not an output violation
implementation: stdlib equality with explicit type policy

concepts.intent: Boolean acceptance requires set(required) ⊆ set(container); extra container values and duplicate counts do not change membership when explicitly allowed.
exclude_or_ambiguous: contains all without multiplicity policy: bind conservatively or unknown
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind container and required argument roles, equality, duplicate policy. Initial support finite list[int]. Argument direction must be explicit.
dimensions_moves: hold required fixed while adding extras
concepts.observable_relation_scope: For the declared iff contract: output == (set(required) <= set(container)). Pairwise monotonicity under adding container values is only necessary, not sufficient; constant True passes monotonicity.
concepts.minimal_contrast: container=[1], required=[1] and container=[1,2], required=[1]. Both True under inclusion; equality implementation differs on second.
concepts.tool_gap_example: Observed accepted-domain cases cover equality only; no row has all required present plus at least one extra container value.
unsupported_failure_modes: set conversion destroys specified multiplicity
Unicode/custom equality assumptions
unsupported required/container types
a wrong equality binding can make a buggy implementation look correct

concepts.intent: For bound eligibility/domain items, output aggregates a predicate by explicit all or any semantics, including declared empty-domain behavior.
exclude_or_ambiguous: each item but unclear eligible domain
empty behavior contradicts usual quantifier: use explicit spec exception
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind item collection, eligible domain, predicate, quantifier, output bool and empty policy. First implementation only audited elementary predicates (integer comparisons/parity).
dimensions_moves: duplicate a witness versus duplicate a counterexample
concepts.observable_relation_scope: all(P(x)) / any(P(x)) over the bound finite domain; observed witness/counterexample counts are measurements. No deduction about unobserved elements or unsupported predicates.
concepts.minimal_contrast: Every value even: [2,4] and [2,3]. all=False on mixed case, any=True. Empty gives True only when the contract says so or unambiguously uses universal semantics.
concepts.tool_gap_example: All tested nonempty inputs have homogeneous predicate truth; no mixed witness/counterexample row.
unsupported_failure_modes: LLM invents P
vacuous-truth assumption conflicts with explicit empty case
short-circuit reach mistaken for semantic forall proof

concepts.intent: Each eligible occurrence contributes its specified weight exactly once to an additive aggregate; optional final comparison is applied to that aggregate. Count uses weight1; sum uses weight x.
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind xs, predicate P, contribution w, neutral0, aggregate result or declared comparison to limit. Initial support int-only count/sum and <,<=,>,>=; no general generated expression DSL.
dimensions_moves: split/join list while holding aggregate fixed
concepts.observable_relation_scope: Aggregate A(xs)=sum(w(x) for eligible occurrences). Decomposition A(a+b)=A(a)+A(b) requires independent eligibility and no length-normalization. For Boolean output do not add booleans; compare independently computed aggregate to the specified bound.
concepts.minimal_contrast: Count x>=limit: ([1],2)→0, ([2],2)→1. Sum positives: [2]→2 and [2,2]→4. At-most predicate: ([0],1) and ([0,0,0],1) must both True if no length rule exists.
concepts.tool_gap_example: No observed eligible equality case; or every observed list length≤2 so length and aggregate effects have not been separated. These are distinct measured gaps, not fault labels.
unsupported_failure_modes: float rounding/overflow semantics
global eligibility depends on other items
sum(set(...)) can combine duplicate and threshold faults
length changes also change sum unless controlled

concepts.intent: Returned sequence respects declared ordering relation and tie policy over its required content. Order obligation does not imply content preservation.
activation: sort by key then secondary key
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind output sequence, key, direction, tie policy. Initial support natural integer order; stability needs distinguishable identity-bearing items and remains outside first diagnostic.
concepts.observable_relation_scope: Adjacent order comparisons and explicit tie relation; Counter content checked separately only when spec requires. Permutation invariance of sorted values needs deterministic order and no identity-dependent ties.
concepts.minimal_contrast: Ascending [2,1] must yield [1,2]; [2,2] distinguishes multiplicity but cannot distinguish direction. Stable key order needs two different records with equal key.
concepts.tool_gap_example: Observed key groups are singleton; no observation exercises an equal-key pair with different secondary values.
unsupported_failure_modes: claiming stability from equal indistinguishable integers
using set-equality as complete sort oracle
tuple/key/identity support not implemented
implementation: no custom ranking compiler in first diagnostic

concepts.intent: Choose an eligible input item according to the stated rule (first, minimum, maximum, or kth), with explicit tie/empty behavior. Eligibility and choice rule must both be bound.
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind xs, P, selection rule and empty outcome. First support first/min/max over int lists; kth and custom identity semantics postponed.
dimensions_moves: move best eligible element after distractor
minimum eligible differs from minimum raw input
add an ineligible element before the current choice
concepts.observable_relation_scope: Output belongs to eligible candidates and satisfies the specified rank/position; empty fallback separate. Eligibility membership alone does not prove optimal/first choice.
concepts.minimal_contrast: Smallest positive: [-1,2,3]→2 vs [-1,0]→declared fallback; [3,2] distinguishes first-positive from minimum-positive. Undefined suitable cannot get an invented exact expected value.
concepts.tool_gap_example: All observed cases have exactly one eligible item; first and minimum remain observationally indistinguishable on that finite set.
unsupported_failure_modes: inferring eligibility from implementation
inventing a rule to resolve ambiguous prose
duplicate identities and total ordering unsupported

concepts.intent: Every input in the declared domain has an allowed outcome category: value, specified sentinel, or specified exception. Bind explicit empty/degenerate clauses without treating every exception as a bug.
activation: return None if no eligible item
all lists are valid with stated return contract
exclude_or_ambiguous: missing empty clause where semantics are genuinely underspecified
concepts.parameters_domain: Bind domain, degenerate condition, allowed outcome and output projection. Timeout is unresolved execution, not evidence of required exception or nontermination.
dimensions_moves: empty raw vs nonempty but empty eligible
exercise declared sentinel and normal branch
concepts.observable_relation_scope: Native return/exception category compared with a spec-justified allowed outcome. Exact nonempty value needs another bound relation; normal return alone does not establish correctness.
concepts.minimal_contrast: Smallest-positive with None fallback: [2] returns2, [0,-1] returnsNone; unguarded min([]) raises ValueError. If spec forbids empty eligible set, the latter is not an admissible counterexample.
concepts.tool_gap_example: Native base runs all return a value on nonempty eligible groups; fallback domain has zero observed executions.
unsupported_failure_modes: domain filter silently excludes declared degenerate inputs
exception captured as opaque text without type
timeouts scored as bugs
no universal totality proof from finite tests
